title: 2-wire transmitter without loop supply
summary: A loop-powered transmitter connected to a passive input has no power: the loop current is 0 mA although the wiring is intact.

sections.heading: What happens
sections.body: A 2-wire transmitter needs the loop to be driven. On a passive input (meant for 4-wire devices) nothing drives it, so no current flows. The input reads 0 mA and, with live-zero diagnostics, reports a wire break that is not one.

sections.heading: How to tell it from a broken wire
sections.body: The wiring checks out end to end, the transmitter display (if any) stays dark, and the drawing shows a 2-wire device while the channel is configured as a passive input. A broken wire shows 0 mA on a correctly supplied loop instead.

troubleshooting.effect: No loop current; the input reports a wire break
symptoms: Wire break diagnostic without a broken wire
evidence: The channel is configured as a passive input
diagnosticMethod: Compare the transmitter type with the channel configuration
repair: Supply the loop (channel setting or external loop supply, as the module manual specifies)
troubleshooting.explanation: Loop power is part of the signal design: decide for every transmitter who powers the loop, and configure the input to match.
